text:
dina: heads-up — since the cilium 1.19 canary in west2 (~40%) we started seeing sawtooth redis/gRPC timeouts on model-train replicas. high retransmit spikes, packets dropped between GPU nodes.
ryan: ugh. which node pools / NIC types are hit? any RDMA in the path?
dina: mostly gpux-large pools, Mellanox cards + SR-IOV. pattern aligns with pods pinned to those nodes. not all nodes, looks patchy.
deploy-bot: cilium-canary: rolled cilium 1.19 to 40% in west2 at 1719995400
sophie: can you capture if GSO/GRO toggles are changing? cilium's offload+encap changes sometimes flip host offload flags. quick checks:
```
# on affected host
sudo ethtool -k eth0 | egrep "gso|gro|lro"
ethtool -k eth0
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -nnnt -s 64 'tcp and (port 6379 or port 50051)'
```
kevin: i suspect interaction between cilium's skb rewrite + SR-IOV offload. if packets are getting fragmented incorrectly it leads to retransmits and RDMA queue stalls. also conntrack entries shown to spike in recent runs.
dina: ran an iperf3 between two affected pods, here's the tail (fresh):
```
[  5]  0.00-10.00  sec  850 MBytes  712 Mbits/sec  1100 ms  2400/23000 (retransmits)
```
ryan: 1100ms?? that's not jitter, that's visible resets. can we repro with host-networked pod to isolate CNI vs infra?
sophie: good call. also dump `cat /proc/net/netstat` and `ss -s` from the host. and `cilium monitor` for policy/encap events.
kevin: temporary mitigation options: 1) disable GSO/GRO on affected hosts (`ethtool -K eth0 gso off gro off`) — will push CPU but should stop bad segmentation. 2) rollback canary to 0% and pin to 1.18. 3) cordon/schedule-away from SR-IOV nodes for latency-sensitive training.
dina: trying ethtool gso off on one node now. will report after a 30m window.
ryan: if ethtool helps we should scale canary → 0 immediately. please also collect `dmesg` for NIC driver errors.
deploy-bot: action: starting canary scale-down to 0% in west2 (initiated at 1719995640)
sophie: note — disabling GSO on RDMA NICs can interact badly with iptables offload. prefer reversing cilium's encap/offload toggle if we can bake a hotfix.
dina: quick logs after gso off — retransmits down ~85%, redis timeouts reduced. so looks tied to host offload interaction.
kevin: that's a pretty clear signal. i'll open an incident ticket and propose rollback + postmortem. who can take the rollback PR?
ryan: i'll own the rollback and the follow-up bisect with cilium-commit ranges.
sophie: follow-ups: add probe that warns when GSO flips on hosts with SR-IOV, add a node-label-based opt-out in our cilium helm values, and schedule a canary with gradual 5% increments and traffic shaping.
dina: opened minimal notes in #incidents and uploaded captures. i'll paste pcap link: https://internal-artifacts/pcaps/1719995555-gso-pktloss.pcap
kevin: created incident INC-2025-42, assigned to eng-infra. rolling back now. cc: networking, ml-infra.
deploy-bot: rollback complete: cilium canary scaled to 0% at 1719995770 — cluster stable checks passing :white_check_mark:
ryan: nice. next steps: bisect, reproduce in a smaller lab with SR-IOV + cilium 1.19, verify kernel + ethtool interactions, and draft mitigations (hotfix + policy).
sophie: add perf cost estimate for disabling GSO across gpux pool. we need that for PM and infra-cost planning.
dina: thanks all — will follow up w/ capture analysis and summary in the incident. :eyes:
